standard.title: Image sequence and meaning
standard.description: Explain how the sequence of images in print, digital and film texts has an effect on meaning
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can explore the effect of choices when framing an image, placement of elements in the image, and colour (AC9E4LA10). They have not yet examined how the ordering and sequencing of images across a text — rather than single-image composition — creates meaning.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students explain how image sequences in print, digital and film texts create meaning through ordering, juxtaposition, and the relationship between images, identifying how sequencing choices affect the reader's or viewer's interpretation.

nodes.label: Images sequence to tell or guide
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify that images in texts appear in a deliberate sequence, and explain how the ordering of images guides the reader's or viewer's path through the text.
nodes.minimum_width: In a picture book or image sequence, identify how the order of images creates a narrative or reading path, and explain how changing the order would change the meaning.
nodes.typical_width: Analyse image sequences in wordless picture books, digital texts with hyperlink choices, and/or short films to explain how ordering guides interpretation. Identify moments where the sequence creates surprise, builds expectation, or controls information reveal.
wider: Compare how image sequences function differently in print (fixed order), digital (multiple possible paths via hyperlinks), and film (time-based) — explaining what each medium's constraints do to meaning-making
Analyse how the sequence of images in texts by First Nations Australian authors create meaning, discussing how image ordering reflects cultural storytelling practices
success_criteria: Identifies the sequence of images in a text and explains how the ordering creates a reading or viewing path.
Explains what would change in meaning if the sequence were altered.

nodes.label: Juxtaposition and relationship between images
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain how placing images adjacent to each other — juxtaposition — creates meaning through contrast, comparison or connection.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one example of juxtaposition in an image sequence and explain what meaning the pairing creates that the individual images do not.
nodes.typical_width: Analyse how juxtaposition is used across several image sequences to create contrast, irony, emotional connection, or narrative development. Explain how the relationship between consecutive images generates meaning beyond what each image contains individually.
wider: Examine how film editing techniques such as cut, dissolve, or match cut create meaning through the juxtaposition of consecutive shots — comparing this to how picture books use page turns to create similar effects
Analyse how image juxtaposition is used in advertising or persuasive texts to create implicit arguments, and discuss the ethical dimensions of that technique

response_modes.reason: Students focus on what individual images contain rather than on the relationship between consecutive images. Encountering juxtaposition across picture book, digital, and film contexts helps students see that meaning emerges from adjacency, not just content — a key conceptual shift.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Juxtaposition as meaning-making applies across wordless picture books, film editing, hyperlink navigation, and advertising — each with distinct conventions. Advancing students can develop a rich cross-media analytical vocabulary around how consecutive images work together.
success_criteria: Identifies two adjacent images and explains the meaning created by their juxtaposition that neither image creates alone.
Names the type of relationship the juxtaposition creates (contrast, connection, comparison, irony, etc.).

nodes.label: Sound and sequence in film
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain how removing or adding sound changes how an image sequence is interpreted, and describe how sound and image sequence work together in film to create meaning.
nodes.minimum_width: Compare an image sequence or film clip viewed with and without sound, and explain at least two ways that sound changes the interpretation of the images.
nodes.typical_width: Analyse how sound (dialogue, music, sound effects) interacts with image sequence in a short film or clip to create meaning, explaining how each element contributes and what is lost when sound is removed. Discuss how interpretation changed between silent and sound viewings.
wider: Examine how music choice in film shapes the emotional meaning of an image sequence, and discuss how the same sequence can be reinterpreted with a different musical score
Analyse a scene where sound and image are deliberately mismatched for effect, discussing what meaning is created by the disconnect

response_modes.reason: Students often say 'the music makes it scary' without explaining the mechanism. A structured reasoning scaffold — 'the sound creates X because it does Y to how we interpret the image' — develops the analytical move from naming to explaining.

success_criteria: Explains at least two specific ways sound changes the interpretation of an image sequence.
Identifies a sound choice (music, dialogue, sound effect) and explains what it contributes to meaning in conjunction with the images.
